newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes rally amid Iraq crisis, grades steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes rally amid Iraq crisis, grades steady.

text.p: U.S. grades rallied sharply fuelled by speculative buying on the back of rising tensions in the Middle East, but grades held mostly steady.
Fears about a possible Iraqi attack on Kuwait, and U.S. ships and planes manuevering into place for a military strike, drove outright prices to an intraday high of $25.30 a barrel.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $25.05-15 a barrel in late trade, some 35 cts higher than Wednesday.
Despite price volatility, grades stabilized after a brief downtrend midweek, helped by the shut Atlantic arbitrage and few North Sea cargo offers with WTI/Brent at $1.09 a barrel.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James held fairly steady in view of the decline in Dated Brent, which was widely expected to affect light domestic grades.
The grade traded between WTI plus 32 and 34 cents, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire drifted lower, moving at plus 20 cents, down about three to five cents from Wednesday.
Gulf Coast refiners are still running at high capacity but remain weary of buying North Sea cargoes because of thin margins for incrementals barrels, traders said.
Heavy, sour barrels were also steady in moderate activity, unfazed by regional offers for Cano Limon and Oriente.
West Texas Sour/Midland was done at $1.17 and $1.16 under the WTI, and Eugene Island at minus $1.06.
